nodes.remediation: Service account: set up domain-wide delegation with the scopes in the Onyx docs, and use a Workspace user as the primary admin. OAuth: connect Google Drive again. Turn on the Google Drive API in the Google Cloud project of the credential.

Make the primary admin a Google Workspace admin, give the service account the admin.directory.user.readonly scope in domain-wide delegation, and turn on the Admin SDK API. Or list the users to index in 'Specific user emails'.
Check the emails in 'Specific user emails': each must be the primary email of an active Workspace user with Google Drive.
To index other users' My Drives, pick a service-account account. An OAuth account reads only what its own user sees.
Service account: make the primary admin a Workspace admin who can manage shared drives. OAuth: the connected user must be a member of the shared drives to index.
Use the URL of each shared drive (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<id>). Service account: an organizer of the drive must be a user Onyx indexes. OAuth: the connected user must be a member.
Use the URL of each folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/<id>). Put shared drive URLs in 'Shared drive URLs'. Share each folder with a user Onyx indexes.
Use each user's primary Workspace email, not an alias. With 'Specific user emails' set, each My Drive email must also be in that list.
Make a Workspace user a Manager of each shared drive, and keep that user in the users Onyx indexes. Without one, Onyx can miss folders with limited access.
Give the service account the drive.readonly scope (OAuth: connect again and accept every permission). A file owner can also block downloads for viewers; Onyx skips those files.
Turn on the Google Docs API in the Google Cloud project of the credential. Without it, Google Docs index without links to their headings.
